thread:
Maya: quick sync — updated autoscale mock posted. goal: make capacity inputs clearer and reduce visual prominence of the burst control. mock: https://redwood-internal.mock/s/autoscale-compact.png

Tom: saw it. quick nit: users confused whether min/max are GPUs or instances. suggest explicit short labels: `Min GPUs` / `Max GPUs` with a helper under the input saying `per-pool GPU instances`.

Maya: yes, short labels + helper text. that fits the compact layout.

Jorge: infra constraints: we treat values as integers for scheduler, so show the unit near input (e.g., `4 GPUs`). also when switching pools we must validate against pool limits immediately.

Rina: accessibility: burst pill contrast is low on small text. also keyboard focus for the number steppers is missing in Safari + VoiceOver.

Leah: recommend three changes: 1) bump burst color to meet 3:1 at minimum (prefer 4.5:1 for body), 2) add visible focus ring and focus-visible class for steppers, 3) ensure steppers expose aria-valuenow/min/max.

Leah: sample aria mapping: 
```
<input id="min-gpus" type="number" aria-label="Min GPUs" aria-valuemin="0" aria-valuemax="100" aria-valuenow="2" />
<button class="stepper" aria-controls="min-gpus" aria-label="increase min gpus">+</button>
```

Jorge: implementation plan: we can keep a custom UI but link it to a visually-hidden native input to preserve keyboard semantics. that also gives us native hold-repeat.

Tom: layout Q: pool selector currently stacked above controls. Can we try compact row: [Pool picker] [Min GPUs] [Max GPUs] [SLO slider]? puts context inline.

Maya: yes — trying inline. watch for long pool names; make picker truncate with ellipsis and expandable full list on click. use aria-expanded / aria-haspopup.

Rina: inline validation when pool change causes conflicts: show a small inline callout: "Pool limit 6 GPUs — your Min is 8." with actions `Reduce to 6` / `Keep`. add role="alert" so screen readers are notified.

Leah: callout must not rely on color only. include an icon + readable text. if we animate in, respect prefers-reduced-motion.

Tom: about burst: suggest moving to a secondary row below inputs with a checkbox `Allow burst capacity` and helper text: `Temporarily exceed Max for spikes.` This de-emphasizes it and reduces accidental toggles.

Leah: checkbox must be keyboard operable and announce state changes. use aria-checked and update a live region when enabling if it affects SLO risk.

Maya: SLO slider copy — change label to `SLO (p95 latency)` and show unit tooltip `ms` on hover. shorter guardrail text: `Lower = stricter. We'll recommend smaller models or quantization when breached.`

Jorge: also add telemetry event `ui.autoscale.poolValidation` when users hit that pool limit callout — helps measure frequency.

Tom: microcopy tweak for the inline Min/Max helper: `Minimum/Maximum number of GPU instances reserved for this pool.` keep it brief.

Leah: I'll do a quick VoiceOver pass tomorrow AM and post issues. primary checks: contrast, focus visibility, aria roles, and announcement behavior for validation/burst toggles.

Maya: next steps: Tom to update the mock with inline picker + secondary burst row; Jorge to prototype hidden native input mapping; Leah to a11y-pass; Rina to refine callout copy. I'll share the new screenshot here when ready.

design-bot: new image uploaded: https://redwood-internal.mock/s/autoscale-compact-v2.png

Maya: thanks all, will loop back once mocks are in.
